prompt:
I need the front end for Snapshelf. A subscription backup service that small offices pay for to keep nightly snapshots of their shared file server, so anyone with access can find and restore earlier versions of files.

Who's using it: Ingrid Solano, 38, office manager at Fernhill & Oduya, an 11-person landscape architecture studio. She chose Snapshelf two years ago and is the de facto IT person. She's competent with file servers but no expert on CAD.

What they're doing right now: It's 9:20 am Monday. Designer Marcus says he accidentally saved over the Linden Park site plan on Friday afternoon, and the client presentation is at 2 pm. She needs to find the right earlier copy of that drawing among many near-identical versions and similarly named files. She has to tell the Thursday version apart from Friday morning's partial edit, check its size and who last saved it, and restore it next to the current file without overwriting anything. Marcus also thinks a planting schedule spreadsheet got clobbered at the same time, so she may need to check that too.

What's in the system at this point: A Synology-style shared server of 1.8 TB is backed up nightly at 1:00 am, with 412 snapshots retained (daily for 60 days, weekly for 1 year, monthly beyond that). The project folder '2026-114 Linden Park' has 1,236 files. Within it, 'LP_SitePlan_v7.dwg' has 9 versions in the last two weeks, ranging from 38.2 MB to 44.9 MB. The Friday 4:51 pm save by m.reyes is 12.1 MB, a suspicious drop. There are similarly named files 'LP_SitePlan_v7_OLD.dwg', 'LP_SitePlan_v6.dwg' and 'LP_SitePlan_v7 (Marcus copy).dwg'. 'Planting_Schedule_LP.xlsx' has 6 versions. Each file version carries a snapshot date, size, last modified by, modified time and file type. Restores done this month: 2, by Ingrid and by Tomoko.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
